doc: What the kernel prints for the host to read: `kith ls --json`, `kith project ls --json` (kernel/bin/kith-project), `kith <agent> --launch-json` (kernel/bin/kith) and `kith ask delegations --json` (kernel/bin/kith-ask). Field names are the kernel's own snake_case. A model or effort is the harness's own word, which the host passes on as it came. Additive only: see serve/contract/README.md.

Harness.doc: The program an agent runs on: `harness:` in its agent.md (`claude-code` is printed as claude), or a backup entry's. The host starts claude, and codex for a backup entry. One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host doesn't start it.

PermissionMode.doc: The Claude Code permission mode a run starts in (kernel/lib/kith_settings.py CHOICES); a Codex run gets the host's translation. One this version doesn't know starts the run in default, which asks before every change.

DelegationState.doc: Where a delegation (one `kith ask` id) stands: `open` (running, or parked on a card), `answered`, `capped` (answered, and its run took the chain to its cost cap) or `stopped` (the run gave no answer). One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host leaves it alone.

Agent.doc: One agent in `kith ls --json`. `home` is its folder, where its bot works. A kernel from before `harness` was listed runs every agent on Claude.

Projects.doc: `kith project ls --json`: every registered project, sorted by id.

Project.doc: One registered project: its paths (absolute), its home folder when it has one, its git remotes, the project it sits in, its shared memory folder, and whether a folder of it is on this Mac.

Launch.doc: `kith <agent> --launch-json`: how to start the agent, for claude and codex. `settings` is Claude Code's settings (null for another harness), `mcp_servers` its servers in Claude's format, `claude_args` the arguments `kith <agent>` would give claude (null for another harness). `backup`, `provider` and `account` say which backup entry, harness and login answer the run; `account_id` is that login as a backup id (`claude`, `claude:work`, `codex`), the agent's main account or the `--backup` entry.

CostTag.doc: What the cost ledger files a run's usage under. `via` is where the run came from (terminal, serve, a channel).

Delegations.doc: `kith ask delegations --json`: every delegation record on this Mac, newest first.

Delegation.doc: The record of one `kith ask` id (foreground, --bg or agent@machine), in kernel/bin/kith-ask's ~/.kith/live/ask/ID.reg. `agent` is the agent asked, `chain` the id of the root ask of its chain, `hop` its depth (0 at the root) and `cross_hops` how many asks of the chain crossed to another Mac. Money is in micro-dollars (US$1 = 1000000) at API prices; `cost_micro_usd` is null for an ask from before costs were kept. `cap_micro_usd` is the chain cap in force now (null: none). `capped_ms` is when this ask's run took its chain to that cap, and `cap_card_ms` when the host raised the Needs-you card for it (once per chain and cap). Times are ms. A record from before delegation records reads as a root ask: chain = its id, hop 0. `brief` is the ask's text (at most 2000 characters) and `session` the asked agent's session once a --bg run claimed one; both are for the owner's peek, null on an older record, and never part of a member's or bot's RPC.

Caller.doc: Who asked: the agent (null for a terminal), the person whose run it is (null for the owner) and where it came from (`terminal`, `serve`, ...).

ReplyTo.doc: Where the answer goes: the caller's session (a wake once nobody waits for it) and the ask whose run asked. This is the only place the address lives; cards never carry it.

launch.doc: How to start `agent` (run in the folder the run works in; `KITH_PERSON` makes it an invited person's run). `backup` launches a backup chain entry instead of the agent's own login; `project` loads that project's context.

delegations.doc: The delegation records on this Mac.
